sections.label: Answering Parliamentary Question
sections.summary: On 20 March 2023, the speaker answered a Parliamentary Question from Mr Leong and Mr Perera.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs and Law (Mr K Shanmugam)
sentences.text: On 20 March 2023, I answered a Parliamentary Question from Mr Leong and Mr Perera.

sections.label: Leong Facebook post and court findings
sections.summary: Mr Leong's Facebook post is called misrepresentation and inaccuracy, while the C3J and DT said the Lees lied under oath.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs and Law (Mr K Shanmugam)
sentences.text: Then, that same night, Mr Leong put up a Facebook post.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs and Law (Mr K Shanmugam)
sentences.text: He said several things including that: one, my characterisation of Mr Lee Hsien Yang and Mrs Lee Suet Fern as having essentially absconded, is inaccurate; two, he also said that by disclosing the investigation into the Lees, Senior Minister Teo and I have risked turning Parliament into "a platform to colour public opinion on criminal proceedings." These statements are a mixture of misrepresentation and inaccuracy, and have to be dealt with.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs and Law (Mr K Shanmugam)
sentences.text: The main points of the answer I gave on Monday, which Mr Leong has avoided, are: first, the Court of Three Judges (C3J) and the Disciplinary Tribunal (DT) have said that Mr Lee Hsien Yang and Mrs Lee Suet Fern had lied under oath and that there was dishonesty.

sections.label: Question on lying on oath
sections.summary: The speaker asks whether the Member agrees the C3J and DT said the Lees lied on oath.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: I am sure the Member can have plenty of time to ventilate at the end.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: I asked a simple question: does he agree that the C3J and the DT have said that Mr Lee Hsien Yang and Mrs Lee Suet Fern lied on oath.

sections.label: Lying on oath and criminal conduct
sections.summary: The speaker asks whether the Member accepts that lying on oath is possible criminal conduct.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai
sentences.text: No, I know it has been said, but I think within the legal interpretation —

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: Therefore, you will agree that the C3J and DT have said that Mr Lee Hsien Yang and Mrs Lee Suet Fern lied on oath.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: Second, Sir, can I ask through you, would the Member accept that, if they did lie on oath, that that is possible criminal conduct?

sections.label: Lees left Singapore, investigations
sections.summary: The speaker says criminal offences must be investigated and the Lees left Singapore and will not return.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai
sentences.text: If there is a criminal offence, of course, it has to be investigated.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: The second point – Mr Lee Hsien Yang and Mrs Lee Suet Fern have left Singapore and have said they will not come back, after being asked to assist in investigations.

sections.label: Police met the Lees
sections.summary: On 9 June 2022, Police met Mr Lee Hsien Yang and Mrs Lee Suet Fern and asked them to assist in investigations.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: On 9 June 2022, Police met Mr Lee Hsien Yang and Mrs Lee Suet Fern and asked them to assist in investigations.

sections.label: Police interview Lee Hsien Yang
sections.summary: Police agreed with Mr Lee Hsien Yang on a 13 July 2022 interview date, but he emailed that day saying they would not attend and had left the country.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: The Police then liaised with Mr Lee Hsien Yang on a suitable date over email and both parties agreed on a date, which was 13 July 2022.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: On 13 July 2022, the day of the interview, they sent an email to the Police saying they would not be attending the interview; by that time, they had left the country.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: From what they have said to the Police and what Mr Lee Hsien Yang has said since, it is clear that they have no intention of returning.

sections.label: Guilty statement withdrawal demand
sections.summary: A Member cites the Cambridge definition of guilty and asks Mr Leong to substantiate or withdraw his statement that they are all guilty.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: The Cambridge dictionary definition of "guilty" is "responsible for breaking a law".

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: So, Sir, I will now invite Mr Leong, through you, to either substantiate his statement, that they are all guilty, or withdraw his statement.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: One cannot, under the cloak of Parliamentary privilege, make these sorts of statements about people.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: And if he does not withdraw, then Sir, we will consider what else needs to be done.

sections.label: CPIB stern warning and prosecution
sections.summary: A Member asks whether a stern warning letter means there is sufficient evidence of guilt but CPIB decided not to prosecute.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai
sentences.text: What the Singapore Court's decision is, we know that the CPIB decided not to prosecute them.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai
sentences.text: But at the same time, we also want to know not to prosecute, does it also mean that in the stern warning letter, there is really —when a stern warning letter is issued, does it mean that there is actually sufficient evidence to show that they are guilty, but there are some reasons that the CPIB decide not to prosecute them?

sections.label: Withdrawal over overseas guilty findings
sections.summary: A Member says he is prepared to withdraw his statement if the Minister said they were not found guilty overseas, noting one person pleaded guilty in the United States.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai
sentences.text: Speaker, if the Minister said that they have not been found guilty overseas, then I am prepared to withdraw my statement.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: Well, for the record, one person pleaded guilty in the United States.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: To the best of my knowledge, no one else has been found guilty.

sections.label: Parti Liyani case relevance explained
sections.summary: A Member says the Parti Liyani case is relevant as a similar case where an investigated person's identity was released and the Member did not object.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: I explained why the Parti Liyani case is relevant.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: It is an illustration of a fairly similar case where we also released the identity of a person who was being investigated and where the Member was present and did not object.

sections.label: Questioning Parti Liyani relevance
sections.summary: A Member asks why the Parti Liyani case is said not to be relevant.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: Why does he say the Parti Liyani case is not relevant?

sections.label: KOM executives non-disclosure comparison
sections.summary: The speaker says they did not object to Karl Liew's disclosure, and the KOM executives' non-disclosure case has not yet occurred.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai
sentences.text: Yes, we did not object to the disclosure of Karl Liew, because it was indeed in the public interest.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai
sentences.text: The case of non-disclosure of the KOM executives has not taken place yet.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai
sentences.text: So, our issue is about the non-disclosure of the KOM executives and the fair treatment between the KOM case and the Lee Hsien Yang case.

sections.label: Withdrawal of Parti Lyani allegation
sections.summary: A Member is asked to withdraw his allegation that Parti Lyani was referred to in order to muddy the waters.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: Will the Member withdraw his allegation that Parti Lyani was referred to, in order to "muddy the waters"?

sections.label: Refusal to withdraw Parti Lyani allegation
sections.summary: The Member refuses to withdraw, and says 38 Oxley Road issues were first made public by Mr Lee Hsien Yang in 2017.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai
sentences.text: Sorry, Speaker, can I ask the Minister to repeat his question?

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: I asked whether the Member is prepared to withdraw his allegation that Parti Lyani's case was referred to, in order to "muddy the waters".

sentences.speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai
sentences.text: Speaker, I am not going to withdraw that.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: Members will recall – issues relating to 38 Oxley Road were first made public by Mr Lee Hsien Yang, himself, in 2017; then in a series of public statements.

sections.label: Facebook post abusing parliamentary privilege
sections.summary: The speaker says a Member who does not raise a point in the House but posts improper and untrue statements on Facebook abuses parliamentary privilege.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: And on the basis that we are all trying to do our best for Singapore, we, through the exchange of ideas and debates, try and get to a point.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: But when someone is in the House, does not raise a point, says that, well, he was digesting it; and then, goes out and puts a Facebook post with both improper statements and untrue statements: then he is abusing Parliamentary privilege, he is in breach of parliamentary rules.

sections.label: Leong's apologies and breaches
sections.summary: Mr Leong apologised in Parliament on 25 February 2021, breached parliamentary procedure on 10 May 2021, and apologised again on 8 March 2022.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: On 25 February 2021, Mr Leong apologised in Parliament for misrepresentations he had made.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: On 10 May 2021, he again seriously breached parliamentary procedure and was told so.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: On 8 March 2022, he again had to apologise in Parliament, for his improper and uncalled for comments.

sections.label: Request to delete post and apologise
sections.summary: The speaker says the Member breached section 31 and asks that he delete his post, accept misrepresentation, and apologise.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: In my view, he has breached section 31.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: That is my view, in the context of his post.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: And Sir, through you, I ask that he deletes his post, accepts that he has misrepresented the position, and he should apologise.

sections.label: Call to delete post and apologise
sections.summary: The speaker invites Mr Leong to delete his post, withdraw the statements and apologise, citing allegations against Senior Minister Teo and himself.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: The allegations against Senior Minister Teo and myself too.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: So, I invite Mr Leong to delete his post, withdraw the statements and apologise, Sir.

sections.label: Statements do not prejudge guilt
sections.summary: Speaking of lying on oath or absconding does not prejudge guilt, as they must return and be charged if Police see fit.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: By speaking about them having lied on oath, as the Courts have said, or them absconding, we do not therefore, prejudge their guilt.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: They will have to come back; they will have to be charged, if the Police see fit to charge.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: As I said in my answer on Monday, when we said that Mr Karl Liew is being investigated for having lied on oath, the comments that were made, we are not prejudging his guilt.

sections.label: Meaning of absconding
sections.summary: Absconding describes running away without cooperating with the Police, and can also mean being fugitives from justice.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: It is a description of the process that they have run away, without cooperating with the Police.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: That is what "absconding" means – run away without cooperating with the Police.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: It can also mean that they have committed an offence of absconding – fugitives from justice.

sections.label: Leong's baseless guilty statement
sections.summary: The only person who made that statement without basis is Mr Leong, who said they were actually guilty.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: The only person who has made that statement without basis is Mr Leong, when he airily said they were actually guilty.

sections.label: Disclosure of names in cases
sections.summary: The speaker says he would not have taken issue with name disclosure in the Lee Hsien Yang case if KOM case names were also disclosed.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai
sentences.text: Speaker, yes, I hope this is the last question.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai
sentences.text: So, I have actually said in my post, I would not have taken issue with the disclosure of names in the Lee Hsien Yang case if names of the individuals involved in the KOM case were also disclosed.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai
sentences.text: As a result, with regard to the Karl Liew case, I take it as normal to disclose in this case, especially when the case became so big and all that.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai
sentences.text: But at that time, I did not know that the Government actually have two mouths.

sections.label: KOM case naming would prejudice individuals
sections.summary: In the KOM case investigations concluded and guilt could not be established beyond reasonable doubt, so naming investigated individuals would prejudice them.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: But for Mr Leong's and the Members' understanding – I had explained some detail the differences, he does not deal with all the differences.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: But in the KOM case, the investigations had concluded.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: An assessment had been made that guilt could not be established beyond reasonable doubt in Court.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: To name the individuals who were investigated under these circumstances would be of prejudice to those individuals.

sections.label: Brazilian court documents individuals
sections.summary: Five individuals were named in Brazilian court documents, but they were not defendants and no court views on wrongdoing were expressed.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: Five individuals were named in the Brazilian court documents.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: But I do not know if Mr Leong knows this – they were not the defendants in that case.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: And as far as I am aware, no views were expressed by the court that they had engaged in wrongdoing.

sections.label: Minister stance on releasing names
sections.summary: The Minister and Government will not release the individuals' names, though the speaker would ask Police to reconsider if the Member states that principle applies to all future cases.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai
sentences.text: Because to and fro, we know what the Minister's stance is and the Government's stance is, that they are not going to release the names of the individuals.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: I am prepared to consider and ask Police to reconsider, if the Member says that is the principle and should apply to all future cases.

sections.label: Release of Lee family names
sections.summary: The release of Mr Lee Hsien Yang's and Mrs Lee Suet Fern's names is on all fours with the Parti Liyani case and other disclosure illustrations.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: Let us move to the release of the names of Mr Lee Hsien Yang and Mrs Lee Suet Fern.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: It is exactly on all falls with the Parti Liyani case and the various other illustrations of disclosure.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: I would invite the Member to go and read carefully what I have said.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: There are situations when you release – and I have explained fully why it was released – and no Member had an issue with that, other than Mr Leong.
